title: Weil positivity on finite windows across L-functions: certified windows, a pre-registered decay law, and an unconditional bound for Dirichlet L-functions
description:
For an L-function and x > 1, let λs(x) be the smallest value of Weil's quadratic form on unit-norm test functions supported in a window of length log x, in the even or odd sector. The Riemann hypothesis for that L-function is equivalent to λs(x) ≥ 0 for every x.

This record contains a technical report with the code and data behind it. The report gives:

  • Certified windows. Arb-certified lower bounds for ζ on windows of support 2.38, 2.6 and 2.99 in both sectors, and certified two-sided brackets for functions without an Euler product.
  • An empirical decay law. Pre-registered tests, with their failures reported, support λ ≈ e−2dT*, T* = 2π(x/Q)1/d, across degrees 1–3. Its conductor collapse discriminates against Zhu's Landau–Widom law transposed to Dirichlet L-functions.
  • A matched pair. The window minimum of the primitive Rédei L-function of (5, 29) is indistinguishable from that of L(χ5)L(χ29), which has the same invariants.
  • Dirichlet characters. An unconditional upper bound for real primitive Dirichlet L-functions, with a Hermite rate proved for all x. It extends to characters and to each sector the bounds Mori proved for ζ.

Nothing here proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis.
